chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajistani told me, saying: Abul-Abbas al-Thaqafi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sabah told us, saying: Jarir informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, from Muawiyah ibn Suwayd ibn Muqran, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited seven things and commanded seven things: He prohibited us from wearing gold rings, and from drinking in vessels of gold and silver, and said: 'Whoever drinks in them in this world will not drink in them in the Hereafter,' and from riding on silk saddles, and from wearing Egyptian silk, and from wearing silk, fine brocade, and thick brocade. And He commanded us (peace be upon him) to follow funeral processions, visit the sick, say 'Yarhamuk Allah' to the sneezer, support the oppressed, spread peace, answer the caller, and fulfill the oath.
Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: Perhaps the correct reading is 'fulfillment of the one who makes the oath'.
ai.seo_question: What are the seven things the Prophet prohibited and the seven things he commanded?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith categorizes practical jurisprudence (*fiqh*) into seven specific prohibitions (*nahi*) and seven recommended acts (*amr*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on both ritual purity and social ethics. The prohibition of gold and silk for men is rooted in the concept of *zuhd* (asceticism) and distinguishing genders, while the recommended acts emphasize communal solidarity, such as *ittiba' al-jana'iz* (following funerals) and *nasr al-mazlum* (supporting the oppressed). This dual structure illustrates the Prophet's holistic guidance, balancing personal adornment with active social responsibility.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-2 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad ibn Ahmad al-Sejezy narrated that Abul-Abbas al-Saqafy quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Abi Ishaq al-Sheibany, on the authority of Ash’as ibn Abil-Sa’esa’ al-Maharebi, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Sowayd ibn Maqran, on the authority of Al-Bara ibn Azib that

God’s Prophet (MGB) admonished the people against seven things and advised the people to do seven things. He (MGB) prohibited us from wearing golden rings; and drinking in golden or silver vessels. He (MGB) said, ‘Whoever drinks in such vessels in this world will not do so in the Hereafter.’ The Prophet (MGB) also advised us against riding on a silk saddle; wearing Egyptian silk clothing; wearing silk garments, fine (colored) silk brocade, and thick brocade.The Prophet (MGB) also ordered us to attend funeral processions; visit the ill; say ‘God bless you’ to one who sneezes; assist the victims of injustice; greet others aloud; accept invitations; and honor our oaths.
Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad (al-Sejezy) added, “It is better to say honor your promise.”
